criteria.evidence: quickQuestionFor picks the first MUST_HAVE EXPERIENCE/SOFT_SKILL with normalised GAP/PARTIAL; test 'the first qualifying must-have experience gap is asked with the three fixed options' asserts req-3, trimmed model wording and the three options.
find() returns undefined -> null; test covers all-MET and SKILL/TOOL/EDUCATION-only gaps.

Array.find returns the first in req order; test asserts req-1 with two qualifying and null (no fall-through) when the first has no wording. Matches the plan and issue wording ('at most one, for the first'); no fall-through is the right call under I.1 (never ask a lesser requirement because the model failed).

Length, trailing '?', empty why, 200-char why and bannedWords are enforced and tested (boundary inclusive). The wording is otherwise unconstrained, so it can embed an unsupported claim or employer name (see finding 1).
quickQuestionFor reads match.status from the normalised requirements map; test 'a normalised gap or partial status...' shows MET with no evidence selected and MET with evidence skipped.

findings.rule: Constitution I.1 / D6 / D21: question and why must never assert a fact about the candidate
findings.trigger: The model sees the candidate facts and returns question 'Besides your time at Infosys, have you presented to senior leaders?' (or why 'You led a team at Acme, so ...') for a PARTIAL must-have. It is under 80/200 chars, ends in '?' and has no banned word, so it is returned verbatim, asserting an employer the posting may not mention. Only the bannedWords blocklist applies; reason got the D21 allowlist but question and why get none.
findings.title: Question text and why are filtered by the blocklist only; no allowlist (D21) stops an embedded employer name or candidate claim
findings.proof: Test: facts with employer 'Infosys', model question 'Besides your time at Infosys, have you presented to senior leaders?' and a PARTIAL SOFT_SKILL requirement; expect question null. Suggested fix: require every content token of text and why to appear in the requirement text (or job text) or a short function-word list, else null; and tell the prompt to word the question only from the requirement.

findings.rule: Scale / constraint: output tokens bounded (PR claims about 100 tokens)
findings.trigger: The prompt asks for a question (80 chars) and questionWhy (200 chars) for every qualifying must-have, up to 40 requirements, but only the first is used. A 40-requirement posting adds up to about 11000 characters (roughly 2800 tokens) to an output capped at 8000 tokens, not about 100; truncation would fail the whole analysis.
findings.title: Prompt requests wording for every qualifying requirement; the PR's 100-token estimate is unsupported

findings.rule: Constitution I.1: prompt does not forbid candidate claims in the wording
findings.trigger: The prompt says 'asking whether the candidate has done it' and 'why the job asks for it' but never says to avoid naming the candidate's employers, titles or facts; the allowed-source rule given for reason ('only words from the cited facts') has no counterpart here.
findings.title: Prompt gives no instruction to keep the question free of candidate facts
